How to use Paradoxe Studio

For a presenter, a creator or an influencer who publishes every week and wants research, script, footage, music and editing in one place, with the AI doing the work and the person keeping the decisions.

Platform detailsContact

Guided tourReal screens

Plays automatically. Use the dots or arrows to move, Pause to stop.

01

Getting started

1

Open Create and describe the episode in one sentence, or paste an article, notes or files.

2

Choose the mode: Auto Production within a budget, Collaborative with a stop at each stage, or Manual.

3

Approve the script, then the storyboard; every generated shot shows its price before anything is spent.

4

Drop your own footage on a scene or let the studio generate it; the first cut assembles itself on the timeline.

5

Adjust in the editor by hand or in plain words, then export the video, the subtitles and an editing package.

02

Features

01

Create

One composer takes a sentence, notes, an article or files and returns a plan: scenes with durations, claims to verify, open questions and the format it chose (monologue, vlog, podcast, explainer).

STEPS

  1. Describe the episode or paste the source
  2. Answer the questions the plan raises
  3. Change type, language or ratio in the side panel
02

Production monitor

Thirteen stages, from research to first cut, each with its status; every scene shows its cost, prompt, references and approval, and can be locked, duplicated, reordered or regenerated. Before any change, an impact preview lists what will move.

STEPS

  1. Pick Auto, Collaborative or Manual
  2. Approve or reject each scene
  3. Approve a priced shot to start its generation
03

Multitrack editor

A preview with safe areas, before and after comparison and full screen, over a timeline of video, overlays, captions, voice and music tracks with waveforms. Edits are made by hand or by instruction, scoped to the selection, the playhead, a track or the whole production, and every one can be undone.

STEPS

  1. Split, trim, move, change speed or add a transition
  2. Or type the change and choose its scope
  3. Undo, redo, or restore an earlier version
04

Music and Sound

A library that knows the difference between a reference and a licence: a streaming link stays a reference until an authorised file is attached, and never plays under its name. Original music is composed in the browser, with tempo detection, ducking under the voice and cuts on the beat.

STEPS

  1. Add a reference or import an authorised file
  2. Record the licence and its scope
  3. Apply ducking or beat sync from Audio tools
05

My Creative Identity

The permanent defaults of a channel: an 8 second opening and a 12 second closing, music for each, look, voice and language, set globally, per show or per project. Finished productions keep what they were made with until the new defaults are applied to them.

STEPS

  1. Choose the level: global, a show or one project
  2. Set opening, closing and music
  3. Apply the new defaults to existing projects if you want
06

Creative Lab and templates

A lab to try looks, hooks and formats before an episode, and a template library built from finished work: any selection on the timeline can be saved and reused as a sequence.

STEPS

  1. Open the Creative Lab from the menu
  2. Save a selection as a template in the editor
  3. Insert it into the next production
07

On the phone

The whole studio works at phone width: a bottom bar for the main pages, a sheet for the rest, and the workspace split into conversation, preview and details.

STEPS

  1. Follow a production from anywhere
  2. Approve a scene or a priced shot
  3. Ask for a change in the conversation
03Tips
  • Start in Collaborative mode; switch to Auto once the defaults sound like you.
  • A budget of zero means the studio asks before every paid generation.
  • Record the licence of every track before publishing; previews of unlicensed music are marked as not for publishing.
04FAQ
Is the studio public?

No. It is my private production tool; a walkthrough is available on request.

Can I get the same studio for my channel?

Yes, set up with your identity, opening, closing, music and connectors. Solo: $2,400 setup, then $149 a month. Pro, with templates, team approvals and a monthly review: $4,900, then $349 a month. Network, for an agency or a group of creators: from $12,000, plus $249 a month per studio.

Who pays for AI generation?

The creator, on their own provider accounts. The studio shows the price of every shot first and spends nothing without an approval or a budget.

Can an editor take over?

Yes. Besides the video, the export contains the subtitles and an FCPXML and EDL package that Final Cut, Premiere or Resolve can open.
